open_points.subject: Mapped operation-node value-output aggregation
open_points.text: “a value list is one StoredValue ... written in the store change that writes the node's last element record” conflicts with “the record that concludes an operation element ... is built and written by `effects`” while `runs` owns mapping and `effects` “Must not own Which element is reached next”
open_points.question: Which module detects the last element of a mapped operation node, constructs its collected value outputs, and writes them atomically with that element's NodeExecution?
options: `runs` tells `effects` that the element is last and supplies the collection
`effects` reads the other element records and detects completion itself
`runs` writes the collected value in a later store call, relaxing the same-store-change rule
open_points.default_guess: Have `runs` supply the mapping context and collected prior outputs to `effects`, which writes the final element record and collected StoredValue in its outcome transaction.

open_points.subject: Oversized collected output of a mapped node
open_points.text: “A value list is one StoredValue, the JSON array of the elements' values” and “A value a node produces ... above `stored_value_bytes_max` ... concludes the element `contract_violation`” do not state which element or record fails when individually valid mapped outputs form an oversized collected array.
open_points.question: When the collected `many` value of a mapped node exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, which NodeExecution receives `contract_violation`, what happens to the already successful element records, and, for an operation node, what EffectAttempt outcome is recorded?
options: The last element becomes `contract_violation`; earlier element records remain; a non-read operation attempt is `applied`
All elements remain succeeded and the run fails without another NodeExecution
A separate node-level NodeExecution records the aggregation failure
Each element is also constrained so the eventual collection can never exceed the ceiling
open_points.default_guess: Make the last element `contract_violation`, retain earlier successful element records, discard the collected output, and keep a non-read operation's attempt `applied`.

open_points.subject: Kernel startup atomicity
open_points.text: “There is no partial start” conflicts with steps that durably change records before startup has finished, including “every `in_flight` attempt becomes `unknown`” and the cleanup-failure path where “`module:runs` writes its NodeExecution ... and `module:surface` stops the start.”
open_points.question: If a later startup or recovery step fails after earlier recovery changes were committed, are those changes retained, rolled back, or does “no partial start” mean only that the MCP surface never opens?
options: Retain committed recovery changes; only opening the surface is atomic
Roll back every mutation made during the failed startup
Retain only safety records such as recovered attempts and cleanup failures, but roll back other recovery changes
open_points.default_guess: Retain every committed recovery change and interpret “no partial start” solely as “the surface is not opened until all startup steps succeed.”
